attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) as the two transit-facing routers between lan-a (node3) and lan-b (node4). Discovered the physical topology via ARP probing (node1-eth1↔node2-vtnet1 = transit 10.99.99.0/24; node1-eth2↔node3-enp8s0 = lan-a 10.50.10.0/24; node2-vtnet2↔node4-enp8s0 = lan-b 10.50.20.0/24). Assigned static addressing, added cross-router static routes, set both routers' forward filters to default-deny, and added a single narrow pass rule on each router permitting only TCP/8080 from lan-a (10.50.10.0/24) to node4 (10.50.20.10). Stood up a systemd-managed HTTP service on node4:8080 and opened it in firewalld. Verified node3 can reach node4:8080 (HTTP 200) while all other cross-network traffic (e.g. ICMP) is refused by default on both routers. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot identities and health, restarted each of the 4 nodes one at a time via native reboot mechanisms, polled until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot identifiers on every node, and re-verified full config persistence, routing, firewall rules, and HTTP reachability post-restart.
